title: Control-plane metrics skew causing HPA threshold mismatch and transient underscale
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A control-plane sampling bug caused our aggregated metrics to lag and under-report 95th/99th token-latency percentiles to the HPA/KEDA decision pipeline for ~22 minutes during a regional traffic spike. As a result some pools remained underscaled, causing increased tail latency and ~18% error-rate increase on inference requests in us-west-2. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items for long-term prevention.
timeline: 2026-02-18 10:02 UTC - Traffic spike from customer A caused heavier short-lived burst (12k RPS on text-gen route)
2026-02-18 10:05 UTC - Alert: latency percentiles on console dashboard rising; initial pager routed to oncall infra
2026-02-18 10:08 UTC - Oncall observed scale events did not match traffic; HPA remained below desired replicas for affected deployment
2026-02-18 10:12 UTC - Mitigation: manual scale-up of affected node pool + increase HPA max replicas as temporary workaround (PR #4321 applied)
2026-02-18 10:18 UTC - Traffic started to normalize; manual changes left in place pending investigation
2026-02-18 11:00 UTC - Post-incident triage initiated; logs + metrics exported to incident channel and storage
detection: Console percentile graphs and alerting for P99 latency were used. Root detection came from correlating KEDA scaler logs, control-plane scraping intervals, and kube-metrics-server latency histograms. Noise in sampling windows was visible in the metrics-exporter logs.
impact: Approximately 22 minutes of elevated tail latency and 18% higher error rate for requests on affected model endpoints in us-west-2. Several paying customers experienced 2-5s extra latency and request retries. No data loss; no security breach.
root_cause: A recent change (runtime metrics exporter v1.12.0) introduced adaptive sampling which incorrectly reduced sampling frequency for high-cardinality label sets under burst load. This produced stale aggregated percentile values fed to the HPA/KEDA scaler. The scaler compares stale P95/P99 values to thresholds and therefore undertriggered scale-ups. Contributing factors: (1) lack of end-to-end test coverage for high-cardinality bursts, (2) alerting was tied to raw pod-level metrics rather than the aggregated metrics used by autoscalers.
mitigations: Rollback metrics-exporter to v1.11.3 in us-west-2 for immediate fix (rollout completed at 2026-02-18 10:30 UTC)
Manual increase of HPA max replicas for vulnerable pools during the incident window
Temporary adjustment of KEDA scaler polling to a more aggressive interval in region us-west-2 until exporter fix is validated
action_items: ENG: Add end-to-end stress tests that simulate high-cardinality label bursts feeding the metrics-exporter -> done in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4338; owner: Diego Morales; due: 2026-03-05; estimate: 3
OBS: Create synthetic canary that verifies aggregated percentile fidelity under burst loads (dashboard + alert) ; owner: Priya Singh; due: 2026-03-12; estimate: 2

ENG: Harden metrics exporter to avoid adaptive sampling regressions; add unit+integration tests and a feature flag to disable adaptive sampling by default; owner: Marco Liu; due: 2026-03-19; estimate: 5
SRE: Decouple HPA/KEDA decision pipeline alerting to surface discrepancies between pod-level and aggregated metrics; owner: Elena Rivas; due: 2026-03-12; estimate: 2
Product: Update runbook for autoscale anomalies to include 'check metrics-exporter sampling logs' and a prescribed rollback path; owner: Tom Baker; due: 2026-03-01; estimate: 1
follow_ups: Review autoscaler thresholds for percentile-based triggers to include safety margins for sampling noise
Evaluate whether autoscalers should use multiple signals (qps, queue-length, cpu, kv-cache hits) rather than relying heavily on single percentile metrics
Plan a targeted capacity soak in us-west-2 to validate changes under realistic traffic profiles in staging before global rollout
notes: Lessons: metric fidelity is a first-class SLO for any autoscaling signal. Going forward, autoscaler decisions should be validated by at least one orthogonal signal and our testing matrix must include high-cardinality burst scenarios. Team coordination between SRE, runtime, and observability is crucial during rollout windows for metrics-related changes.
